content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I am looking to use a 0-10v signal and [product_name] to monitor the status of animal feed bins across several locations. Is it feasible to monitor this data online, or could [product_name] trigger an output that sends a text message whenever a bin needs refilling?

One straightforward approach with [product_name] is to wire an output to an SMS alarm device. I've implemented this many times using an SMS alarm module from Conrad, for example: [url]. This setup can also detect power interruptions and notify you by SMS. If you have ethernet access, you could use a [product_name] model with ethernet and connect it to a router or through the internet, allowing you to monitor remotely using [product_name] software.

analysis.insight_summary: The user wants to enable remote monitoring of animal feed bins using [product_name], with alerts via SMS or online updates about bin levels. Suggestions include integrating outputs with third-party SMS alarm modules or utilizing ethernet-enabled [product_name] hardware and corresponding software to achieve remote monitoring and notifications. The key focus is reliable, automated reporting across locations.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipates that the [product_name] system will deliver dependable real-time monitoring and automatic notifications, such as SMS alerts, when bins require refilling on multiple remote sites.
